findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Restate the live-conflict step so it stages a genuine BOTH-SIDES divergence — a rebar-side body edit AND a Jira-side edit against a shared previously-converged baseline — matching 3388's 'both sides edit the same body' precondition, since a bare Jira-side edit is suppressed by the directionality guard (outbound_field_diff.py:248-258) and yields Jira-wins with no outbound-field-conflict, not local-wins.
evidence: Plan Approach: 'performs a Jira-side edit to assert 3388's settled concurrency behavior: the next pass keeps rebar's body (local-wins) AND surfaces the divergence as the existing deduped outbound-field-conflict bridge alert'

outbound_field_diff.py:354-362 records a conflict only when `fname in _INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS and not _local_matches_baseline(...) and not _remote_matches_baseline(...)` — i.e. BOTH sides diverged from baseline
outbound_field_diff.py:248-258 `_suppressed_by_inbound`: when local is unchanged since baseline, the differing remote is left for the inbound differ (Jira-wins), not local-wins clobbered
Ticket 3388's own AC/Testing name the precondition exactly: 'both sides edit the same body' / 'A concurrent both-sides body edit keeps rebar's body (settled local-wins)'
findings.finding: The live-conflict scenario ('a Jira-side edit between passes keeps rebar's body local-wins AND raises outbound-field-conflict') under-specifies the precondition the cited 3388 policy actually requires: the outbound-field-conflict alert fires only on a BOTH-SIDES divergence (local!=baseline AND remote!=baseline). A bare Jira-side edit with local unchanged is suppressed by the directionality guard and mirrored inbound (Jira-wins) with NO conflict alert.
findings.location: Approach (3rd bullet: 'performs a Jira-side edit'); Testing ('Live conflict'); Acceptance Criteria (2nd checkbox)
scenarios: The live test performs only a Jira-side edit (no divergent local edit) between passes: the directionality guard suppresses outbound, the inbound differ mirrors Jira's value, rebar's body is REPLACED (not local-wins), and no outbound-field-conflict is emitted — the AC's assertion cannot hold.
A reviewer reading the AC believes a pure remote edit proves local-wins, freezing an incorrect mental model of 3388's policy.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the scenario to: (1) converge the body so a baseline is recorded; (2) make a rebar-side local edit to the description AND a Jira-side edit to the same field before the next pass; (3) assert the next pass emits rebar's body (local-wins) and records the deduped outbound-field-conflict:<key>:description alert. This mirrors 3388's test_concurrent_conflict_alerts precondition (local!=baseline AND remote!=baseline).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the exact renderedFields HTML/macro shape is UNVERIFIED and specify how the test derives its expected markup — either probe DC 8.17.1's actual `renderedFields.description` output first and pin observed tokens, or assert tolerantly (e.g. presence of a bold element regardless of `<b>`/`<strong>`, a heading element, and a code macro/`<pre>`), rather than hard-coding an assumed tag shape.
evidence: Plan: 'asserts rendered HTML through ?expand=renderedFields ... (*foo*→bold, h1.→heading, {code}→macro). No renderedFields/expand= assertion exists in the harness today, so this is a genuinely new fidelity check.'

Endpoint surface EXISTS (Partially-verified): expand=renderedFields is corroborated by the repo's own captured live Jira responses — tests/fixtures/jira/search.json:5 and tests/fixtures/jira/live_ground_truth/REB-458_issuelinks.json:1 both carry `"expand": "renderedFields,names,..."`; and dc_request/_request (tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:81) already issues query-string GETs, so the request is plumbable.

Specific markup shape UNVERIFIED: those same fixtures show `"renderedFields": null` (tests/fixtures/jira/search.json:382,799,...) — no capture actually requested the expand, so the concrete DC-rendered HTML (e.g. `<b>` vs `<strong>`, the heading tag, the code-macro wrapper) is not observed anywhere in the repo.

This is the story's stated residual risk ('the real Jira DC wiki renderer ... differ from pandoc and cannot be modeled offline — that gap is the residual risk this story closes'), so a live assertion is the right vehicle; only the hard-coded markup tokens are the concern.
findings.finding: The plan asserts specific rendered-HTML markup (bold/heading/code-macro) from the live DC renderer via `?expand=renderedFields`, but the exact HTML/macro serialization DC 8.17.1 emits is unverified: the harness has never requested renderedFields (the repo's captured Jira responses all show `"renderedFields": null`), so the concrete tag shape the assertion keys on is unknown until the instance is probed.
findings.location: Approach (1st bullet) + Acceptance Criteria (1st AC): '?expand=renderedFields ... *foo*→bold, h1.→heading, {code}→macro'
scenarios: DC renders bold as `<strong>` rather than `<b>` (or wraps headings/code-macros in a container the assertion did not anticipate), and the new fidelity test fails on markup shape rather than on a genuine codec defect — a false red on the very check that is supposed to be the live proof.
The test is written against remembered/assumed HTML and silently over- or under-matches, weakening the fidelity claim it is meant to establish.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope `test_normalize_rich_text_contract` to the DELTA the existing `test_richtext_port*.py` tests do not cover — the public `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` import path and signature/return-type back-compat that `agentic-dev-platform` depends on — and note the existing behavioral coverage so the new test does not merely re-assert decode/passthrough already pinned.
evidence: Plan: 'Add a contract test that pins the public shape/behavior of normalize_rich_text ... so a change that would break the agentic-dev-platform import fails here first.'

Existing tests already pin behavior: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_richtext_port.py (test_normalize_rich_text_decodes_adf_dict, test_normalize_rich_text_passes_string_through) and test_richtext_port_heldout.py (test_normalize_rich_text_never_returns_a_dict, test_normalize_rich_text_handles_empty), both via _backend().inbound.normalize_rich_text.

The plan's stated intent is distinct (a back-compat pin of the PUBLIC import path InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text for the sibling repo agentic-dev-platform), which the existing port tests do NOT frame as an import-surface/signature guard — so the new test is legitimately additive, but its scope is not differentiated from the existing behavioral coverage.
ABSENCE: the plan does not cite the existing test_richtext_port*.py coverage nor state that the new test targets only the import path/signature (not re-asserting decode/passthrough behavior).
findings.finding: The proposed cross-repo `normalize_rich_text` contract test overlaps in surface with existing behavioral coverage that already pins the same function's decode/passthrough/empty/never-dict behavior; the plan does not acknowledge this coverage or scope the new test to the delta (public import-shape / signature back-compat).
findings.location: Approach / Scope / Testing / AC3 — the `normalize_rich_text` contract test (`test_normalize_rich_text_contract`)
scenarios: Author writes test_normalize_rich_text_contract re-asserting ADF-dict decode and string passthrough, duplicating test_richtext_port.py rather than adding the distinct import-surface/signature guarantee.
A future refactor changes the port-role tests and the contract test drifts to assert the same thing twice.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach/Testing, add one sentence noting that decode/passthrough/empty/never-dict behavior is already pinned by tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_richtext_port.py and test_richtext_port_heldout.py, and that test_normalize_rich_text_contract adds only the cross-repo import-surface guard: import via the public `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` binding and assert the callable's signature/return type (str) that agentic-dev-platform relies on.
